reviewer_lane: fresh independent source and assertion-quality review
scope: New guest Settings T28, T40, and T67 acceptance paths and focused comparator assertions. No downstream capture or full extension reload credit is inferred.

targets.target: T28 matches the source case for visible guest section roster and opening/closing without preference writes.
targets.evidence: The source Collapsible exposes aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-hidden, and inert; SettingsView has the exact 11 guest groups and Data/SEO each render 'No options yet'. The driver enumerates the exact roster, observes open/closed semantics and checks a before/after digest of persisted Settings. It repeats after the panel reload boundary.

targets.target: T28 proves actual content visibility follows the trigger state.
targets.evidence: contentNonempty only proves the mounted content has text. The remaining assertions inspect aria-hidden and inert, but never computed visibility, layout/clip geometry, or an equivalent visible-content observation. Since Collapsible keeps children mounted while closed, these assertions can pass while the CSS visibility behavior is broken.

targets.target: T40 verifies the guest preference control and persisted value through both switch states and panel reload.
targets.evidence: Each trusted click is followed by an aria-checked and chrome.storage.local value comparison, and the same state is checked after reloadSettings. The case explicitly records downstream page-load capture as unverified. This does not establish that background capture consumes the setting.

targets.target: T67 verifies both mode selections through reload.
targets.evidence: The real picker is clicked for each mode, then its displayed label and stored scrapeAutoMode are compared before and after reloadSettings. No capture-quality claim is made.

findings.finding: The T28 visibility contract is weaker than its name and case brief. The test never observes that the content is actually visible while open or visually hidden while closed; aria-hidden/inert are accessibility semantics, not a rendered-visibility assertion, and contentNonempty remains true for the mounted closed content.

Both per-section finally blocks click back when necessary but do not wait for or assert restoration of the recorded initial expanded state. A failed run can therefore leave the section in an unverified state while reporting only the original failure.

If UI already equals the baseline while storage differs, cleanup skips the click and then times out; it does not repair the persisted value. This is precisely a plausible failure state when persistence is the broken behavior under test. T67 has the analogous same-selection issue if the UI shows the baseline while storage differs: selecting the already-selected option may not trigger a write.

The new focused tests exercise only pure matcher functions with hand-constructed state objects. They do not invoke the native driver, real click/reload sequence, or persistence observer, so they are comparator self-checks rather than forcing guards on the browser path. No executed mutation or local test run is claimed in this review.

limitations: The current source-only review does not establish that a native acceptance run passed on an artifact containing these changes.
T40 background capture behavior remains unverified by design; no downstream capture or full extension reload credit is granted.

positives: The control drivers use the shared trusted CDP click helper and compare visible control state with the real chrome.storage.local Settings payload.
The test explicitly keeps T40 capture behavior unverified and does not claim scrape integration.
The comparator predicates reject mismatched visible/stored values, a missing control, altered section roster, and changed settings digest.
required_repairs: For T28, assert rendered visibility for open and closed content, and verify restoration to each section's recorded initial state in cleanup.
Make T40/T67 cleanup restore baseline even when the displayed value matches but persisted storage does not; verify the restored value after a reload.
Add a forcing check at the acceptance seam, or keep the helper unit tests clearly supplemental and do not treat them as browser-path regression coverage.

commands_run: Source inspection of SettingsView, Collapsible, persistence store, case brief, inventory, and acceptance harness
limits: No local tests, browser, build, or extension reload were run, as instructed.
Only this assigned review report is authored by this reviewer.
